about.title: Carson Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical care in Carson happens at a fast clip. Roughly 93,000 people live here, and many more pass through on the 405, the 91 and Avalon Boulevard every day, so clinics, urgent-care offices and nearby hospitals across Los Angeles County stay busy. Most visits go fine. When they don't, the harm can be quiet at first: a lab result nobody followed up on, a medication mix-up, a surgical problem that only shows itself weeks later. California's MICRA framework governs these claims, and it is stricter than an ordinary injury case. You generally have one year from the date you discovered the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to file. A 90-day notice must go to the provider before suit. A qualified medical expert almost always has to confirm that the care fell below the accepted standard, because a bad outcome by itself is not malpractice. Our team handles medical negligence claims on contingency, at no upfront cost to you.

items.title: MICRA Deadlines Are Short
items.desc: California gives you one year from discovering the harm and never more than three years from the injury, plus a 90-day notice requirement before filing. Acting early keeps those windows open.

items.title: Expert Review Is Built In
items.desc: A qualified medical expert is almost always needed to show the care fell below the standard. Our team handles that step so you don't have to hunt for one yourself.

items.title: Free to You, Contingency for Us
items.desc: We charge nothing upfront, and we work on contingency. MICRA caps non-economic damages at a figure that rises each year, and we can explain how that applies to your case.

items.question: I was treated in Carson but the hospital is in Torrance or Long Beach — does that change anything?
items.answer: Not in terms of the law. MICRA applies statewide, so the same discovery rule, 90-day notice and expert requirement govern wherever in California the care happened. Because Carson sits in Los Angeles County, a claim would ordinarily be handled through the county's court system, and we can sort out the venue details.

items.question: My surgery didn't go well. Is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law requires more than a poor result — a qualified medical expert must show the provider did something a reasonably careful professional would not have done. Many complications happen even with proper care. We can review your records and tell you honestly whether the facts support a claim.

items.question: How long do I have to act after discovering a medical error?
items.answer: Generally one year from when you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and no later than three years from the injury itself. You also have to send the provider a 90-day notice of intent before filing suit. Those timelines can overlap in tricky ways, so reaching out soon is wise.
